advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure `_is_archived_ticket` detects net-ARCHIVED state for COMPACTED tickets (whose ARCHIVED event is folded into a SNAPSHOT / renamed to `*.json.retired`), not only raw-`.json` tickets.
evidence: src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:30-31 `for fname in os.listdir(ticket_dir): if fname.startswith(".") or not fname.endswith(".json"): continue`
src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:41 `if etype == "ARCHIVED" and uuid:`
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:302 `# I1: RENAME folded sources to ``*.retired`` rather than deleting them.`
A compacted ARCHIVED event becomes `{ts}-{uuid}-ARCHIVED.json.retired`, which fails the `.endswith(".json")` filter, so no ARCHIVED uuid is collected and `_is_net_archived` returns False.
advisory.finding: The archived-ticket scope exemption does not fire for COMPACTED archived tickets: `_is_net_archived` only inspects raw `*.json` files for `event_type=="ARCHIVED"`, but compaction renames folded events to `*.json.retired` and folds their state into a SNAPSHOT, so a compacted archived ticket's ARCHIVED event is invisible and `_is_net_archived` returns False (ticket scanned normally). Compacted archived tickets are exactly the population carrying the null-commit ledger entries this change targets.
scenarios: A ticket is archived and later compacted; its ledger holds signed events but the ARCHIVED marker is now `.retired`, so the gate still scans it instead of exempting it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Gate `_is_net_archived` behind the `.archived` marker precheck (as `reduce_all` does) so non-archived tickets skip the full event re-parse.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:151 `return _is_net_archived(ticket_dir)`
src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:258 `if exclude_archived and os.path.exists(os.path.join(entry_path, ".archived")):` then `if _is_net_archived(entry_path):`
src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:30-36 `_is_net_archived` reads and `json.load`s every `.json` file in the ticket dir.
advisory.finding: `_is_archived_ticket` invokes `_is_net_archived` unconditionally on every ticket, whereas the canonical caller only calls it behind a `.archived` marker-file precheck. This makes the whole-store gate perform a full `os.listdir` + JSON-parse of every event file for EVERY (mostly non-archived) ticket, adding per-ticket I/O the change otherwise aims to remove.
scenarios: Whole-store `--all` gate over a large store: every ticket now pays an extra parse-all-events pass just to determine archival.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (and document/test) that classifying unresolvable-commit ledger entries VERIFIED via any-key — which includes revoked keys — is acceptable, or narrow it to keys that were valid at some point / add an audit signal.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:245-246 `if commit_sha is None and not is_live: return VERIFIED`
src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:535-536 `The trust root is built from EVERY keyring record's public key — regardless of ``revoked_at``` (verify_authorship_any_key)

Commit message acknowledges the trade-off: `a resolvable-but-wrong-era key still fails; LIVE events keep fail-closed behavior`, but a revoked key on an UNRESOLVABLE ledger entry is not distinguished from a valid one.
advisory.finding: An authentic-but-unresolvable LEDGER entry is classified VERIFIED via an any-key verify that includes REVOKED keys, so a signature by a compromised/since-revoked key on a null-commit, unresolvable-position ledger entry now passes the gate (era-scoping is skipped entirely).
scenarios: A compromised key is revoked; an attacker crafts/injects a SNAPSHOT ledger entry with null commit_sha and an unresolvable position signed by that revoked key — it classifies VERIFIED under enforcement.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align merge handling between `build_position_commit_map` (`--no-merges`) and the `resolve_position_commit` fallback, or document why the fallback intentionally includes merges.
evidence: src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:390-393 map uses `--full-history --no-merges --no-renames`
src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:159-163 `resolve_position_commit` uses `--diff-filter=A --full-history` WITHOUT `--no-merges`
advisory.finding: `build_position_commit_map` uses `--no-merges`, but its per-entry fallback `resolve_position_commit` does not, so a position whose only add appears in a merge commit is a map-miss and then resolves (differently) via the merge-including fallback — a subtle inconsistency between the batched map and the fallback resolver.
scenarios: An event file introduced only inside a merge commit: absent from the map, then resolved to the merge commit by the fallback, yielding a commit the map deliberately excludes.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the `commit_sha is None and not is_live → VERIFIED` branch cannot be reached with a revoked-key signature (verify_authorship_any_key ignores revoked_at), and that the unresolvable-commit condition is not attacker-forceable via snapshot ledger position/commit_sha.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:245-246: `if commit_sha is None and not is_live:` then `return VERIFIED`

verify_authorship_any_key trust root is built from EVERY key regardless of revocation — authorship.py:535-537: "The trust root is built from EVERY keyring record's public key — regardless of ``revoked_at``"

commit_sha for a ledger entry comes from the recorded position/commit_sha, which are snapshot data an attacker can set — the held-out test does exactly this: `entry["position"]["commit_sha"] = None` and `entry["position"]["position"] = f"9999999999999999999-{euuid}-NEVER-COMMITTED"` (tests/unit/test_identity_gate_archived_and_unresolvable_heldout.py) then commits the edited snapshot

Reachability: a signature by a revoked (post-revocation, wrong-era) key with a null/unresolvable commit is now accepted as VERIFIED, whereas the prior code returned KEY_NOT_VALID_AT_ERA (unverified). Enforcement is advisory today (rebar.toml:97 `require_authenticated = false`) but forceable on via `--require-authenticated` (verify_authorship.py:503).
advisory.finding: An authentic-but-unresolvable LEDGER entry is reclassified from KEY_NOT_VALID_AT_ERA to VERIFIED whenever its introducing commit cannot be resolved and the signature verifies against ANY key the identity has ever held — including REVOKED keys — bypassing the era/revocation guard. The unresolvable-commit condition is forceable via attacker-controllable snapshot ledger fields (position/commit_sha).
scenarios: A snapshot authorship_ledger entry is signed with a key that was later revoked; commit_sha=null and position is set to a value that resolves to no committed file; the gate classifies it VERIFIED instead of key_not_valid_at_era.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that an attacker-appendable ARCHIVED event removing a ticket (and its unsigned/forged events) from the authorship gate's scope is an acceptable trust boundary, or gate archived-scope exemption on an authenticated signal.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:410-413: `if _is_gate_exempt_ticket(ticket_dir) or _is_archived_ticket(ticket_dir):` ... `continue`

_is_net_archived is computed purely from scanning the ticket dir's ARCHIVED/REVERT events — reducer/_api.py:26-47: iterates fname in ticket_dir, `if etype == "ARCHIVED" and uuid: archived_uuids.add(uuid)` ... `return bool(archived_uuids - reverted_uuids)`
The held-out test asserts an archived ticket's (unsigned) events are absent from the gate report: tests/unit/test_identity_gate_archived_and_unresolvable_heldout.py `assert archived_entries == []`
advisory.finding: Net-ARCHIVED tickets are removed entirely from the authorship gate's scope, and the archived determination is derived from the ticket's own event files (unauthenticated tickets-branch data). Appending an ARCHIVED event to a ticket drops ALL of that ticket's events — including unsigned/forged/wrong-era ones — out of gate scope.
scenarios: An attacker (or a compromised/unauthenticated writer) appends an ARCHIVED event to a ticket that also contains unsigned or forged events; the whole ticket then drops out of the enforcement gate's scope.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add regression tests for the unresolvable-ledger carve-out negatives: a forged signature over a null-commit unresolvable ledger entry must stay BAD_SIGNATURE, a LIVE event with an unresolvable commit must stay key_not_valid_at_era, and a resolvable-but-wrong-era ledger entry must stay key_not_valid_at_era.
evidence: Code carve-out under review: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:245-246 `if commit_sha is None and not is_live:` → `return VERIFIED`
Code's own stated guardrails (verify_authorship.py:238-244): 'a forgery still fails; a resolvable-but-wrong-era key still fails; LIVE events keep fail-closed behavior'

The only new test for this branch asserts the authentic path: test_identity_gate_archived_and_unresolvable_heldout.py:164 `assert not report` / :165 `assert res.returncode == 0` — no negative case where the signature is a forgery over an unresolvable ledger entry, nor a LIVE event with unresolvable commit.

ABSENCE: existing forgery/era tests (test_identity_ts3_117b_heldout.py:120,146) sign LIVE events (rebar.comment / hand-written CREATE), never a compacted null-commit LEDGER entry, so they do not exercise the new `commit_sha is None and not is_live` gate and cannot detect it over-firing (regression blindness).
advisory.finding: The new authentic-but-unresolvable carve-out (`if commit_sha is None and not is_live: return VERIFIED`) is regression-tested only on its happy path; the three guard conditions the code comment says it must NOT swallow — a forgery (BAD_SIGNATURE), a LIVE event with an unresolvable commit (KEY_NOT_VALID_AT_ERA), and a resolvable-but-wrong-era ledger key (KEY_NOT_VALID_AT_ERA) — are not tested against this new ledger-null-commit branch, so a widening of the carve-out that force-VERIFIES a forged or wrong-era ledger entry would not be caught.
scenarios: A future refactor drops the `not is_live` predicate or the `if not any_v.verified: return BAD_SIGNATURE` short-circuit; a forged or wrong-era ledger entry is silently classified VERIFIED and the new happy-path test still passes.
A compacted ledger entry signed by a key the identity never held (forgery) with an unresolvable position is admitted as VERIFIED.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the held-out file with three tests mirroring the existing harness: (1) reuse test_forged_signature_is_bad_signature's Mallory-signed event but route it through the compacted-ledger null-commit + unresolvable-position setup, asserting the verdict is `bad_signature` and the gate fails; (2) a signed entry whose position stays resolvable but whose key was revoked-before-era, asserting `key_not_valid_at_era`; (3) a LIVE (uncompacted) signed event whose position cannot resolve, asserting it does NOT get the ledger VERIFIED carve-out.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that exercises a successful build_position_commit_map hit — assert it maps a known event's position to the oldest introducing commit (matching resolve_position_commit) so a mis-keyed/empty map is caught rather than masked by the fallback resolver.
evidence: New function build_position_commit_map derives the position key via `position = base.rsplit("-", 1)[0] if "-" in base else base` (authorship.py, added block) — untested key-derivation logic.

New test forces a map MISS: test_identity_gate_archived_and_unresolvable_heldout.py:150 sets `entry["position"]["position"] = f"9999999999999999999-{euuid}-NEVER-COMMITTED"` (no committed file matches), so `position_map.get(ev.position)` at verify_authorship.py:554 returns None and the fallback at :556 runs.

ABSENCE: no test references `build_position_commit_map` or `position_map` (search over tests/ returned no matches); the existing test_ledger_null_commit_sha_reresolves_to_verified (test_identity_gate_scope_and_ledger.py:175) keeps a real position but its assertion (`not report`) is satisfied by EITHER the map hit OR the fallback resolver, so it cannot detect a map that returns `{}` or a wrong-keyed entry.
advisory.finding: The new `build_position_commit_map` function has no test that exercises a successful map HIT: the sole new test that drives the gate's position-map path deliberately corrupts each entry's position to an id no committed file matches, forcing a map MISS and the per-entry fallback resolver, so the function's position-key derivation and record parsing are never validated on a real hit; the pre-existing null-commit test cannot distinguish a map hit from the fallback, so a broken map would be masked.
scenarios: A regression in the position-key derivation (e.g. an event TYPE that is not dash-free, or an off-by-one in rsplit) makes `build_position_commit_map` return wrong or empty keys; the gate silently falls back to the per-entry O(n) resolver — correctness preserved but the stated performance fix is silently defeated, and no test flags it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that commits a few real events, calls `authorship.build_position_commit_map(repo_root=...)`, and asserts the returned dict maps each event's `{timestamp}-{uuid}` position to the same sha `resolve_position_commit` returns for that position (and that a non-existent position is absent).
